items.title: [ckan] CKAN: Session Fixation in Registration View
items.summary: DescriptionWeb user registration form is vulnerable to session fixation if the site is configured with server-side session storage (CKAN uses cookie-based session storage by default). The attacker would need to either set a cookie on the victim's browser or steal the victim's currently valid session. Session identifiers are now regenerated after registration.PatchesThis vulnerability has been fixed in CKAN 2.10.11, 2.11.6 and 2.12.0Workaroundsswitch to cookie-based session storage (the default) or disable web user registration by setting ckan.auth.create_user_via_web to false (the default)Referenceshttps://github.com/ckan/ckan/security/advisories/GHSA-6499-jgj4-2wpfhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-104773https://github.com/ckan/ckan/commit/6eae4e9c430e163b9d6cc75a3fd2ca82e79d80f6https://github.com/ckan/ckan/commit/8f8e8b587461b66120ec7a85c17a34ecea213f57https://github.com/ckan/ckan/commit/a25e2f3080a79a94eb04dcf02e16ded3e5fadeb2https://github.com/ckan/ckan/commit/c30bae7fdd616d98a5d47cc31f9e8d5d1ad7bcd2https://github.com/ckan/ckan/commit/c72815a5afd50cf689fcfb688f431dec21a85915https://github.com/ckan/ckan/releases/tag/ckan-2.10.11https://github.com/ckan/ckan/releases/tag/ckan-2.11.6https://github.com/ckan/ckan/releases/tag/ckan-2.12.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6499-jgj4-2wpf

items.title: [amqtt] aMQTT: Denial of Service (DoS) via Memory Leak in Unmanaged QoS 2 Session Handshakes
items.summary: Impactamqtt is vulnerable to a remote denial of service caused by incomplete MQTT QoS 2 transactions remaining allocated after the associated client disconnects.MQTT QoS 2 uses a four-step handshake to provide exactly-once delivery. If a client begins a QoS 2 transaction but disconnects before the handshake completes, amqtt retains the associated transaction state and packet identifier without an expiration mechanism to remove it.QoS 1 transactions are protected by a timeout mechanism, which defaults to 5 seconds, allowing abandoned state to be released. Equivalent timeout handling was not applied to incomplete QoS 2 transactions.An attacker can repeatedly connect to the broker, initiate QoS 2 transactions, and disconnect before completing the handshake. Each incomplete transaction leaves state allocated in memory. Repeating this process causes broker memory consumption to grow continuously.Successful exploitation can cause:Unbounded growth in broker memory usageAccumulation of incomplete QoS 2 transaction stateIncreasing memory pressure on the host systemTermination of the broker process when available memory is exhaustedOperating-system Out-Of-Memory (OOM) interventionComplete loss of availability for the affected broker processExploitation does not require maintaining long-lived connections. An attacker can create incomplete QoS 2 transactions and disconnect, leaving the broker to retain the associated state after the network connection has closed.Under the default configuration, anonymous clients can exploit the vulnerability without credentials. When authentication is enabled, any authenticated client permitted to initiate QoS 2 message flows may still be able to exploit it. Authentication alone is therefore not a sufficient mitigation.Ecosystem: pipPackage: amqttAffected versions: >= 0.11.0, <= 0.12.0The vulnerable code is present in the v0.11.0 release commit, 352678c87e50e501a8a5bb91fab73c9400fa046c, and remained present on the main branch as of 5ebbf366f6b79ab12a06f426ffd18ff28954e4ea. Versions before 0.11.0 were not evaluated.This is a denial-of-service vulnerability only. No confidentiality or integrity impact has been identified. Successful exploitation causes degradation and eventual loss of availability through memory exhaustion.PatchesThe issue will be been patched in the v0.12.1 released version; all users should upgrade.The completed fix:Apply transaction expiration handling consistently to incomplete QoS 1 and QoS 2 message flowsExpire abandoned QoS 2 state when the associated transaction does not complete within the configured timeoutRelease the associated message state and packet identifiers when the transaction expiresPrevent disconnected clients from leaving incomplete QoS 2 transactions resident in broker memory indefinitelyThe fixing commit is 2755fd801a6f95e9b73e11116948b57a95348466WorkaroundsAdministrators who cannot immediately upgrade should limit the ability of untrusted clients to create large numbers of incomplete QoS 2 transactions.Where application requirements permit, preventing untrusted clients from using QoS 2 provides the strongest temporary mitigation.Connection and request rate limiting at a reverse proxy, load balancer, firewall, or other network layer can reduce the rate at which an attacker creates abandoned transactions, but does not eliminate the underlying vulnerability. An attacker able to continue creating incomplete QoS 2 transactions can still cause memory usage to increase over time.Administrators should also monitor broker memory consumption and configure appropriate process or container memory limits to prevent exhaustion of host resources. Restarting the broker may reclaim abandoned state and restore availability, but the broker remains vulnerable until the patched version is installed.MQTT Keep Alive limits are not a sufficient mitigation because the vulnerable state persists after the client connection has already terminated.Referenceshttps://github.com/Yakifo/amqtt/security/advisories/GHSA-wcqj-wx85-c75phttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-130176https://github.com/Yakifo/amqtt/pull/404https://github.com/Yakifo/amqtt/commit/2755fd801a6f95e9b73e11116948b57a95348466https://github.com/Yakifo/amqtt/commit/64a6f8c3ebc47640f2e092885c1d504c8f34f1afhttps://github.com/Yakifo/amqtt/releases/tag/v0.12.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wcqj-wx85-c75p

items.title: [amqtt] aMQTT: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity and Uncontrolled Resource Consumption and Improper Input Validation
items.summary: Impactamqtt is vulnerable to a remote denial of service caused by improper MQTT topic-filter validation combined with catastrophic regular-expression backtracking.A single client can freeze the entire broker by sending one specially crafted SUBSCRIBE packet followed by one PUBLISH packet.The vulnerability is caused by two defects:add_subscription() validates the placement of the single-level wildcard + using substring checks for /+ and +/, rather than verifying that each /-delimited level containing + is exactly +. This allows malformed filters such as "+/" + "+" * 60 to be accepted instead of rejected with return code 0x80, as required by MQTT-4.7.1-3._matches() converts every + character into the greedy regular-expression fragment [^/]* and evaluates the resulting expression with re.fullmatch(). A filter containing many adjacent + characters can cause catastrophic backtracking when matched against a topic that partially matches but ultimately fails.Topic matching runs synchronously inside the broker’s global broadcast loop. When the malicious match is evaluated, it blocks the asyncio event loop and prevents the broker from processing any other work.The issue was reproduced using a single raw MQTT 3.1.1 TCP connection with no third-party client dependencies.Successful exploitation causes:Existing message delivery to stopNew MQTT connections to receive no CONNACKKeepalive processing to stopBroadcast processing to stopThe broker to remain unavailable until the process is restartedUnder the default configuration, anonymous clients can exploit the vulnerability without credentials. When authentication is enabled, any authenticated client permitted to create arbitrary subscriptions and publish messages may still exploit it. Authentication alone is therefore not a sufficient mitigation.Ecosystem: pipPackage: amqttAffected versions: >= 0.11.0, <= 0.11.3The vulnerable code is present in the v0.11.0 release commit, 352678c87e50e501a8a5bb91fab73c9400fa046c, and remained present on the main branch as of eeb1e254da9a1e8d9cc68ae754fcedac652e8fc0. Versions before 0.11.0 were not evaluated.This is a denial-of-service vulnerability only. re.escape() prevents arbitrary regular-expression injection, and there is no known path to remote code execution.No confidentiality or integrity impact has been identified. Successful exploitation causes a complete loss of availability for the affected broker process.PatchesThe issue has been patched in the v0.11.4 released version; all users should upgrade.The completed fix:Validate topic filters one level at a timeRequire any level containing + to be exactly +As part of comprehensive MQTT topic-filter validation, require # to occupy an entire level and appear only as the final levelReplace the regular-expression matcher with deterministic, level-by-level MQTT topic matchingSimply changing the validation logic is not sufficient defense in depth if malformed filters can reach the existing regular-expression matcher through another code path.WorkaroundsThis is the temporary mitigation that was recommended prior to the patched release: administrators can install a topic-filtering plugin that rejects malformed wildcard subscriptions before they are added to the broker. Place the plugin in an importable Python module, enable it in the broker configuration, and restart the broker.from amqtt.contexts import Actionfrom amqtt.plugins.base import BaseTopicPluginfrom amqtt.session import Sessionclass RejectInvalidTopicFilters(BaseTopicPlugin):    """A plugin to prevent invalid wildcard subscriptions."""    async def topic_filtering(        self, *, session: Session | None = None,        topic: str | None = None,        action: Action | None = None    ) -> bool | None:        if topic and action == Action.SUBSCRIBE:            levels = topic.split("/")            return all(                level in {"+", "#"} or ("+" not in level and "#" not in level)                for level in levels            ) and "#" not in levels[:-1]        return True        config = {    ...    'plugins':{        ...        'myplugins.RejectInvalidTopicFilters': {}    }}This workaround applies when subscription requests pass through the plugin. If the broker is configured to use a persistent session plugin, restarting the broker alone is not sufficient; any persisted sessions containing malformed topic filters need to be removed.Restarting the broker restores availability after exploitation, but the broker remains vulnerable until the patch or workaround is installed.AcknowledgmentsaMQTT thanks the following security researchers for their professional, coordinated private disclosure:Yongkang Xiao (Wuhan University)Min Shi (Wuhan University)Qiyi Deng (Wuhan University)Jing Chen (Wuhan University)Referenceshttps://github.com/Yakifo/amqtt/security/advisories/GHSA-2hjf-7455-w946https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-104199https://github.com/Yakifo/amqtt/pull/361https://github.com/Yakifo/amqtt/commit/e48a8a65027667f936d415db
